title: The 7 Most Powerful Moats for AI Startups: speed first, then Helmer's seven powers applied to AI
summary: Garry Tan and the Light Cone hosts apply Hamilton Helmer's 7 Powers (process power, cornered resources, switching costs, counter-positioning, brand, network economies, scale economies) to AI startups. Garry's core message is to find a painful problem and move fast first, since moats only matter once you have something worth defending.

principles.text: Find a real person with a real problem and solve it first; moats come later.
principles.quote: this is sort of why we generally tell people to go find a person with a real problem and then go solve that problem first.

principles.text: Moats are for scaling a working business; don't pick or drop ideas based on forecast moats, speed is the first moat.
principles.quote: all the things that we're about to cover, aside from speed, are sort of one to a billion, one to 10 billion, one to a hundred billion, one to a trillion-dollar sort of problems.

principles.text: Start with a specific person whose pain is severe and existential, not a nice-to-have.
principles.quote: You should start with do I have a specific person who has some sort of pain point and it's pretty painful.

principles.text: Forward-deployed engineering builds a cornered resource: real customer data and workflows nobody else has.
principles.quote: they're going out and getting a cornered resource in the form of real data and real workflows. Literally sitting with a customer who normally would never get access to good software.

principles.text: Superior engineering is the most profound modern process power; use code gen to scale it.
principles.quote: One way to look at it is way better engineering is actually that's like the most profound form of process power.

principles.text: AI vertical SaaS can capture far more wallet share by charging for the work done rather than software seats.
principles.quote: because you're not like 1% of wallet share, you can get to 10.
